subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the lines (x + 2a)² − 3y² = 0 and x = a form an equilateral triangle, and find the area of that triangle.

mark_split.label: Split the pair into two lines
Show the three sides are equal

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 4 PAIR OF STRAIGHT LINES, Short Answer question 15(ii), book p.171. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split is 1+1+1+1 because this question is answered by direct coordinates rather than by angles: split the pair, find the two vertices on x = a, compare the three side lengths, then compute the area. Each of the four is a separate result on the page. This card proves the shape by SIDE LENGTHS, not by angles, which is a different route from its companion question 15(i) and is the shorter one when the vertices are this easy to write down. The area was cross-checked a second way, as ½ × base × height with base BC = 2√3|a| and height 3|a|, which also gives 3√3a². Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say where the pair of lines meet, and how you show the three sides are equal.

steps.label: Split the pair into two lines
steps.margin_note: First mark. The pair is a difference of two squares. It is NOT homogeneous, so the two lines do not pass through the origin — they meet at (−2a, 0), which is the third vertex.
steps.memory_tip: This pair is not homogeneous, so the two lines meet at (−2a, 0) and not at the origin.
lines: (1) is a difference of two squares:

recall.must_convey: That the pair splits as (x + 2a − √3y)(x + 2a + √3y) = 0 and both lines meet at (−2a, 0).
accept: it is A squared minus B squared so it factorises as A minus B into A plus B
the two lines are x plus two a minus root three y and x plus two a plus root three y
both lines meet at minus two a comma zero
difference of squares ga factorise cheyyali
multiply the factors back to check

steps.why: Setting both factors to zero at once gives y = 0 and x = −2a, so that point lies on both lines and is the vertex the pair contributes. Take a ≠ 0 here: if a were 0 the line x = a would pass through that same point and there would be no triangle at all.
common_mistakes: Assuming the pair passes through the origin because it has no xy term.

steps.label: Find the other two vertices
steps.margin_note: One mark. The third line is vertical, so put x = a straight into each factor. Both give 3a on the left, and only the sign in front of √3y differs.
steps.memory_tip: x = a makes x + 2a equal 3a in both lines, so only the sign of the y term changes.

recall.must_convey: That putting x = a in the two factors gives B = (a, √3a) and C = (a, −√3a).
accept: put x equals a into each of the two lines
x plus two a becomes three a in both
the two vertices are a comma root three a and a comma minus root three a
x equals a substitute chesthe rendu vertices vasthaayi
three a over root three is root three a

steps.why: The two vertices sit at equal distances above and below the x-axis, so the triangle is symmetric about the x-axis before any length is measured.
common_mistakes: Taking x = a as y = a and looking for a horizontal line.

steps.label: Show the three sides are equal
steps.margin_note: One mark. BC is vertical, so its length is just the gap between the two y values. AB and AC are equal by the symmetry about the x-axis, so only one of them needs the distance formula.
steps.memory_tip: BC is vertical, so its length is just the gap between the two y values.
lines: ∴ AB = BC = CA, so △ABC is equilateral.

recall.must_convey: That all three sides come out equal to 2√3|a|, so the triangle is equilateral.
accept: B C is vertical so its length is the gap between the y values
A B squared is nine a squared plus three a squared which is twelve a squared
all three sides are two root three mod a
moodu sides equal ga vasthaayi so equilateral
A C equals A B by symmetry about the x axis

steps.why: Equal sides is a complete proof on its own — no angle has to be measured once all three lengths agree.
common_mistakes: Measuring BC as √3a, which is only the distance from B to the x-axis.

steps.label: Find the area
steps.margin_note: The last mark. With the side already known, the equilateral-triangle area formula finishes it. The same answer comes from ½ × base × height with base 2√3|a| and height 3|a|.
steps.memory_tip: Area of an equilateral triangle is (√3/4) × side squared, and here side squared is 12a².

recall.must_convey: That s² = 12a² and (√3/4)s² gives the area 3√3a² sq.units.
accept: area of an equilateral triangle is root three by four into side squared
side squared is twelve a squared
the area is three root three a squared square units
equilateral triangle area formula vaadali
root three by four into twelve a squared is three root three a squared

steps.why: The area carries a² and not |a|², because squaring the side removes the modulus: |a|² and a² are the same number for every real a.
common_mistakes: Writing the area of an equilateral triangle as ½s² instead of (√3/4)s².
